ann_22.original: Hypothesis: this part is the model's tally of first values. Nine one-hot columns reach the score through their own edges, summed in identity_direct, and the first level of a1, a2, a4, a5 and a6 each lowers that sum by a similar step, so the more attributes sit at their first value, the lower the score. Prediction (self-probe): starting from the case with every attribute at its second level, where the direct sum is 33.9, moving a single attribute to its first value lowers the direct sum to 14.7 for a1=1, 11.5 for a2=1, 16.4 for a4=1, 9.7 for a5=1 and 15.1 for a6=1; the model does this. a3 is the exception: its direct edge (on a3:2) runs the other way, and a3=1 raises the direct sum to 39.2; the first-value cost of a3 is carried by the a3_a6_chain part instead. The other levels move the sum much less: a2=3 gives 36.9, a5=3 and a5=4 give 29.8 and 29.8, and a1=3 gives 33.9, the same as a1=2 (33.9), because a1 has no direct edge on its third level. Edge weights per sd of the z-scored column, directly through each edge: a1:1 -9.19, a2:1 -8.56, a4:1 -8.11, a5:1 -8.75, a6:2 9.43 (a6 has two levels, so a6=1 is the low end of this column), a3:2 -2.63, a2:2 2.03, a2:3 3.45, a5:2 1.80. The part is linear, so the sum is the weighted sum of these columns; get_formula's rounded closed form is off by up to 0.027 on the training rows. Switching the part off (its exit held at its training mean) changes training accuracy from 41.2% to 32.8% and flips 29 predictions; the probability AUC reported by the same query falls from 0.616 to 0.537, the largest loss of the three parts.
ann_22.proposed: This part adds a direct term for each attribute: a2 = 1 or a4 = 1 lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' for the typical case from about 72% to below 1%, moving a1, a5 or a6 away from its first value raises it to above 99%, and its a3 term runs the other way, lowering it to about 1% for a3 = 2.

ann_23.original: Hypothesis: two units, each with a single input edge from an a3 column, that make a small a3 offset, against the main a3 effect. Unit 2445 reads a3:1 and is off: 0 of the 345 training rows have node_2445 > 0, and at both a3 levels its value is 0.0 and 0.0, so it adds nothing. Unit 639 reads a3:2 and is on in 100% of the training rows (node_639 > 0 for 345 rows), so its ReLU never cuts and it acts as a linear a3 term. Prediction (self-probe): the part should push the score up for a3=1 and down for a3=2. At the case with every other attribute at its second level, node 639 is 1.04 at a3=1 and 5.36 at a3=2, and through its negative output weight the part adds 1.52 to the score at a3=1 and -1.60 at a3=2, relative to its training mean; the model does this. The offset is small next to the a3 switch in a3_a6_chain, which moves the score the other way. Switching the part off changes the mean predicted risk by 0.010 and training accuracy from 41.2% to 42.3%. get_formula's rounded closed form is off by up to 0.0037. parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: this chain is how the model charges a3's first value. Gate 435 is an a3 switch, on when a3=2 and off when a3=1, and while it is on it lifts the chain's output by a large amount; units 821 and 1957 pass that on, with smaller terms for a6 and for a1=3. Gate 435 is on in 168 training rows, and 168 training rows have a3=2; 0 rows with a3=1 have it on and 0 rows with a3=2 have it off. Unit 1083 (reading a3:1 and a6:2) is never on in training: 0 of the 345 training rows have node_1083 > 0, and its value is 0.0, 0.0, 0.0 and 0.0 at the four a3 and a6 combinations, so its edges into 435 and 821 carry nothing. Units 821 and 1957 are on in 100% and 100% of training rows, so they act linearly. Prediction (self-probe, a3 crossed with a6 at a1=2, a2=2, a4=2, a5=2): at a3=2, a6=2 node 435 is 3.33 and the chain outputs 54.9; at a3=1, a6=2 node 435 is 0.00 and the output falls to 24.3, a drop of the same order as one first value's step in the direct terms. a6=1 lowers the output a little, to 51.3 at a3=2 and 20.8 at a3=1. confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients
